# Sparrow of Home Health (`sparrow-of-home-health`)

Checks home health 30-day periods: notices of admission missing or late (with the payment cut per day), periods that overlap, visits outside any period, and periods that ended or are ending under the low-utilization visit threshold. Patient names are masked before results reach the model.

**Sparrow never files notices of admission. Sparrow never submits or changes claims.**

Kestrel ver 1 · Specialty billing · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`kestrel-core`](../kestrel-core)

```bash
npx -y sparrow-of-home-health demo
npx -y sparrow-of-home-health mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up home health agency, made-up patients. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`periods.csv`](fixtures/periods.csv) and [`visits.csv`](fixtures/visits.csv). Planted:
  - S1: the notice of admission for the October 1 start of care was filed October 9 (due October 6), so the period payment is cut by 8/30.
  - S2: start of care November 3 with no notice of admission (due November 8).
  - S3: the period that ended October 14 had 2 visits against a threshold of 4.
  - S4: the second period starts November 1, inside the first (which runs to November 3), and a visit on September 30 falls before any period.
  - S5: the period ends November 18 with 2 visits against a threshold of 5.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): 5 days for the NOA, a 180 average per-visit payment for the low-utilization estimate, and a 7-day warning. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `sparrow_check` | List missing or late NOAs, overlapping periods, stray visits and low-utilization periods. | runs |
| `sparrow_write_report` | Write sparrow-home-health.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and sparrow-home-health.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/sparrow). | runs |
| `sparrow_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `sparrow_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `sparrow_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `sparrow_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `noa_submit` | Sparrow never files notices of admission. | refused |
| `claim_submit` | Sparrow never submits or changes claims. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `sparrow_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `periods` (required) | 30-day periods under --root: patient, period start and end, admission (Y for the start of care), NOA filed, LUPA threshold, expected payment |
| `visits` (required) | Visit log: patient, visit date, discipline |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: noa_days, lupa_default, per_visit_rate, warn_days |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx sparrow-of-home-health inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### 30-day periods (`periods`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `start` (required) | date | Period Start, Start, Start Date, From, Episode Start, Period From |
| `end` | date | Period End, End, End Date, Through, Thru, Episode End, Period To |
| `admission` | text | Admission, Start of Care, SOC, First Period, Admit Period |
| `noa_filed` | date | NOA Filed, NOA Date, NOA Submitted, NOA Accepted, Notice of Admission |
| `lupa_threshold` | number | LUPA Threshold, LUPA, Visit Threshold, Threshold |
| `payment` | amount | Expected Payment, Payment, Period Payment, Expected, Amount |
| `payer` | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Insurance, Insurance Name, Plan, Plan Name, Payor |

### Visits (`visits`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `date` (required) | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `discipline` | text | Discipline, Visit Type, Service, Type |

## Settings file (`sparrow_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `noa_days` | Calendar days to file the notice of admission; default 5 |
| `lupa_default` | Low-utilization threshold when a period has none; default 2 (thresholds run 2 to 6 by case-mix group) |
| `per_visit_rate` | Average per-visit payment, to estimate the loss on a low-utilization period; default 0 |
| `warn_days` | Days before a period ends to warn about low visits; default 7 |

## Memory

`sparrow_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `sparrow_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `kestrel-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sparrow-of-home-health": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "sparrow-of-home-health",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add sparrow-of-home-health -- npx -y sparrow-of-home-health mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
sparrow-of-home-health tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
sparrow-of-home-health sources               # the columns each input is read from
sparrow-of-home-health inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
sparrow-of-home-health call sparrow_check '{"periods":"<periods>","visits":"<visits>"}'
sparrow-of-home-health eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
sparrow-of-home-health demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
